To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the vector-vector and scalar- vector self-interactions have no significant impact on the properties of infinite nuclear matter, but they do affect the surface properties, in particular the symmetry energy and the surface tension.

the model based on a vector-vector self-coupling and a scalar-vector self-couplings is able to reproduce the nuclear matter properties as well as the surface properties in a similar manner as the standard non-linear $\omega$ model.

the inclusion of vector-vector and scalar- vector self-interactions in the relativistic mean field model leads to a more realistic description of nuclear matter and surface properties, in comparison to the standard non-linear $\omega$ model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the surface properties of nuclear matter within the framework of a relativistic mean-field approach.

the model studied here is a very promising candidate to be used in nuclear structure calculations.

the present model with scalar-vector and vector-vector self-interactions is able to reproduce the nuclear matter properties of the standard non-linear $\omega-\sigma$ model, but it is not able to reproduce the surface properties of this model.
the inclusion of the scalar-vector and vector-vector self-interactions in the mean field approach does not lead to an improvement in the description of nuclear matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model is a good candidate to describe nuclear matter, but it is not a good candidate to predict surface properties.

the model is able to reproduce the bulk properties of nuclear matter, and the nuclear matter saturation point can be obtained for reasonable parameter values, which is not the case for the standard model with vector-vector and vector-scalar self-interactions only.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the inclusion of vector-vector interactions in a non-linear $\sigma-$ model leads to surface properties that are in better agreement with empirical data, in particular for the nuclear symmetry energy, than those of the standard $\sigma-\omega-\rho$ model.
the inclusion of vector-vector and scalar vector self-interactions is not sufficient to describe nuclear matter.
the inclusion of vector-vector self-interactions in a relativistic model of nuclear matter is essential to obtain a realistic description of nuclear matter.
